references.text: Continuation of the same theme where God repeats that he is the Lord who brought Israel out of Egypt, and that they shall be holy because he is holy.
The same command regarding holiness: 'You shall be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy.'
Repeats the command to consecrate themselves and be holy because the Lord is their God.
God calls Israel to be holy because he is holy, and he has set them apart from the nations.
Israel is called to be a holy people for the Lord, a kingdom of priests.
Israel is a holy people for the Lord and chosen to be his treasured possession.
The seraphs cry out 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts', which emphasizes God's holiness.
Peter quotes directly from this text: 'Be holy, for I am holy' (ἅγιοι ἔσεσθε, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἅγιος).
Paul writes that God's will is sanctification (ἁγιασμὸς ὑμῶν), which reflects the call to holiness.
The exhortation to pursue holiness (ἁγιασμόν), for without it no one will see the Lord.
